If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over the last 5 days, adjust mid-horizon (days 8–15) forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect momentum reversal.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) in the last 5 days, reduce late-horizon (days 16–30) forecast by 0.5–1.0% to hedge against erratic behavior.

If sentiment is uniformly positive but forecasted price is >10% above recent high, reduce late-horizon forecast by 1–2% to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is uniformly negative but forecasted price is <10% below recent low, increase late-horizon forecast by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound potential.
